answer: Payment sits in escrow until a panel grades the work, and a tie or a suspicious score sends the same submission to a second panel drawn from a different budget line, so the payout waits while the review repeats. Because a farm cannot collect until both panels agree, the attacker's cash sits idle across the ocean of queue time and every karst of duplicate accounts needs its own escrow, which turns a fast delta of fake rewards into a slow, capital-hungry trickle.
